decisions.reason: F10 originally cites only the density-operator trace law, which neither identifies the unit-vector state with its rank-one density operator nor evaluates the trace as a squared coordinate. This is a missing dependency at step 2.1, not a failure of the calculated witness. Replaced F10 and its dependency by thm-qa-19-measurement-distribution, whose proof constructs the basis PVM and evaluates tr(P_phi P_y). The hypotheses hold: both graph generators are Hermitian and the input is unit. The sign witness has p_+(1)-p_-(1)=2 sin(1) cos(1)>=5/6; the irregular path has transfer times pi/sqrt(2) and pi. No refuted statement changes.

The procedure defines exact supplied whole-operation and ordered local-operation branches and terminates after n local calls and one measurement. A separate result is the correct place for correctness. In thm-qa-19-hypercube-transfer-correctness, step 1.1 constructs the common tensor eigenbasis; step 2.1 proves the chronological product U_X_(n-1)(t)...U_X_0(t)=U_A_n(t) by multiplying eigenphases on every basis vector, including the empty identity product for n=0. Steps 3.1-5.1 establish transfer and measurement. Thus the promised equivalence is already proved, and no algorithm edit is needed.

F5 and step 5.2 attribute the invariant block to the cited theorem, while the contract quotes only its Statement of exact/approximate success. The theorem proof does compute the same block in step 1.1, and the example independently establishes orthonormality, invariance, every matrix entry, K^2=I/N, and the gap 2/sqrt(N) in steps 1.1-4.1; thus this is a nonfatal citation-scope defect, not a circular or invalid matrix derivation. Reworded F5 to the theorem's actual exact-success conclusion and step 5.2 to apply that conclusion to the uniform input, retaining the local derivation. N=2 gives [[-1,-1/2],[-1/2,0]] and gap sqrt(2); the n=1,2 Hadamard preparations are correct. The Example and all Statement/Definition interfaces remain unchanged.
